feedback:
The candidate is valid. All sensor positions are inside the allowed x and y ranges, sensor_size 0.008 is an allowed option, the weights are antisymmetric in [-2, 2], and kp, ki, kd, base_speed and line_loss are in range. Nothing is obviously broken. It is a reasonable response to iteration 0, where all 60 trials ended off_track with one line-loss event each (progress 0.04 to 0.115, max_error about 0.061). Those failures came early, so the first priority is keeping the robot on the tape. The candidate targets that by moving to 8 mm sensors, lowering kp from 3.0 to 2.0, raising kd from 0.05 to 0.2, and lowering base_speed from 1.7 to 1.5. The changes are made together, so the race will not show which one matters most.

Two risks to watch. (1) base_speed 1.5 gives a PWM base of about 0.75. The course needs an average of roughly 1.5 m/s to finish in 3.0 s, so the robot may stay on track and still time out or stall without completing. (2) kp 2.0 gives a weaker correction per unit of signal. If the robot stays on track but drifts wide on bends, the gain is too low, not too high.

This is early exploration with 10 iterations left, and the candidate is a sensible step from a field that has not yet completed a track. Approving gets telemetry, which will sharpen the next critique more than another round of review on numbers alone. The next revision should depend on what the race shows, as set out in the requested changes.
requested_changes: If the race shows max_error still above 0.06 with line_loss_events of 1 or more and progress stalling early, go back toward kp 2.5 with kd 0.2 and keep the 8 mm sensors. Iteration 0 showed the 0.06 m off-track limit is reached early, so the line must be kept on the bends.

If the robot stays on track but completion_time is above about 2.8 s or the run ends by stall with progress well below 1, raise base_speed in steps (1.5 to 1.7) while keeping kd at 0.2. Iteration 0 needed about 1.5 m/s to finish, so speed is then the limit.

If line_loss_events stays at 1 per run with the line lost on the first bend, try line_loss 'search_right' or 'search_left' in place of 'last_direction' before changing the gains, to test whether the search direction is the cause.
